item.research_question: How to develop high-performance potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) via advanced design strategies and engineering?
item.material_system: Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs), including various electrode materials such as carbon-based materials, alloy-based electrodes, oxides, sulfides, selenides, and Prussian blue (PB) and its analogs
key_findings: Nanostructured design can improve the K+ reaction kinetics and enhance the rate capability and cycling performance of PIBs
Buffering volume changes using a carbon matrix can improve the cycling stability of PIBs
Heteroatom doping can enhance the kinetics and increase the defects and vacancies in PIBs
Regulating salt chemistry and electrolyte additives can minimize side reactions and K dendrite growth in PIBs
Electrode design can enhance the energy density of PIBs
item.mechanism: The authors propose various strategies to address the challenges in PIB research, including nanostructured design, buffering volume changes, heteroatom doping, regulating salt chemistry and electrolyte additives, and electrode design
item.limitations: The authors mention that further experimental work and in-depth discussion are needed to completely understand the correlation between structure/doping effects and their electrochemical properties
item.future_work: The authors suggest several possible directions for advanced PIB research, including developing advanced electrode materials, optimizing electrolytes, improving battery safety, and designing full-cell PIBs
quotes: Approaching high-performance potassium-ion batteries via advanced design strategies and engineering
PIBs have attracted tremendous attention due to their low cost, fast ionic conductivity in electrolyte, and high operating voltage
Further investigation should consider graphitic carbon anode to explore suitable graphitic microstructures with long stable cyclability as well as high tap density for commercial application
